1	# Method Context: First Vacuum-Plus-Wall External-Region Capability
2	
3	This task does not use a single journal paper. Instead, it provides condensed
4	method context extracted from the TERPSICHORE to DESC native migration work
5	used to author the benchmark.
6	
7	## Scientific setting
8	
9	The relevant transition is:
10	
11	- from plasma-only internal stability analysis;
12	- to plasma plus vacuum-region analysis;
13	- and then to plasma plus vacuum plus conducting-wall analysis.
14	
15	Task 008 is about the first stable step in that transition: moving from a
16	reduced internal-only setting to a vacuum-plus-wall external-region setting.
17	Once a conducting wall is part of the problem, the native code must not only
18	carry more geometry. It must represent a different external region.
19	
20	## Key ideas
21	
22	1. The vacuum region is modeled as a pressureless, shearless pseudo-plasma.
23	2. The vacuum region uses extra pseudo-flux surfaces `ivac`.
24	3. The plasma-vacuum interface must remain geometrically consistent.
25	4. The wall enters the external-region geometry rather than acting as a
26	   cosmetic flag.
27	5. Wall geometry changes the vacuum metric reconstruction.
28	6. The vacuum metric feeds an outer-region operator path.
29	7. That operator path must influence reduced response assembly and therefore the
30	   interval-level energy accounting.
31	
32	## Reduced outer-region chain
33	
34	For this reduced benchmark slice, the outer-region capability can be thought of
35	as three consecutive translations:
36	
37	1. `VACMET`-style geometry reconstruction produces wall-sensitive metric fields
38	   on the pseudo-vacuum intervals.
39	2. Those metric fields are projected into reduced modal families that carry
40	   the wall-sensitive Fourier content of the vacuum region.
41	3. The reduced families are then assembled into outer-shell interval matrices
42	   that feed the same global energy reduction used by the internal plasma
43	   path.
44	
45	The important benchmark point is that changing the wall should not stop at step
46	1. It must propagate through all three translations and survive into the final
47	interval-energy accounting.
48	
49	## Structural cues in the source
50	
51	The public source snapshot intentionally retains the plasma-side analogs for
52	the same kinds of operations:
53	
54	- modal lookup and sum/difference indexing in the coefficient path;
55	- block-level potential assembly in the plasma path;
56	- final global energy reduction from interval blocks.
57	
58	The missing outer-region capability is therefore not "invent a brand new
59	solver." It is "rebuild the external-region translation path so wall-sensitive
60	geometry actually reaches the operator and energy layers."
61	
62	## Why this matters
63	
64	If adding a vacuum region plus wall still leaves the code behaving like the
65	internal-only scaffold, then the external-region capability has not actually
66	been established. The physical issue is not just one geometry array. It is the
67	missing propagation from wall-coupled external geometry into the vacuum-side
68	metric, operator, and energy chain.
69	
70	## What the source snapshot contains
71	
72	The reduced snapshot keeps a real package shape for:
73	
74	- radial grids and mode tables;
75	- equilibrium-to-boundary adaptation;
76	- VACMET-style pseudo-vacuum metric construction;
77	- vacuum coefficient mapping;
78	- plasma/vacuum block assembly;
79	- interval-energy reduction.
80	
81	The task is to restore the first wall-sensitive external-region capability in
82	that chain without hard-coding one reproduction case.

352	    fppp = np.asarray(profiles.get("fppp", np.zeros_like(profiles["ftp"])), dtype=float)[interval]
353	    ci = np.asarray(profiles["ci"], dtype=float)[interval]
354	    cj = np.asarray(profiles["cj"], dtype=float)[interval]
355	    pp = np.asarray(profiles["pp"], dtype=float)[interval]
356	    sqgbsq = cj * fpp - ci * ftp
357	    if abs(ftp) < 1e-14:
358	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero ftp denominator.")
359	    if abs(sqgbsq) < 1e-14:
360	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero SQGBSQ denominator.")
361	    if np.any(np.abs(sigmab) < 1e-14):
362	        raise ValueError("FOURIN grid functions encountered near-zero sigmab denominator.")
363	    gsplm = (sigbs / sigmab - fpp * gstl) / ftp
364	    if modelk in {1, 3}:

415	    """Accumulate one-interval ``cna``/``cnb`` from FOURIN grid functions.
416	
417	    This ports the visible summation loops after ``A0..A11`` construction in

431	    cnb = np.zeros((7, lss_with_sentinel))
432	    cna[1] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a2"], dtype=float)
433	    cna[2] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a6"], dtype=float)
434	    cna[3] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a7"], dtype=float)
435	    cna[4] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a5"], dtype=float)
436	    cna[5] = tsc @ bjac
437	    cna[6] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a0"], dtype=float)
438	    cnb[1] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a1"], dtype=float)
439	    cnb[3] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a4"], dtype=float)
440	    cnb[4] = tss @ np.asarray(functions["a10"], dtype=float)
441	    cnb[2] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a3"], dtype=float)
442	    cnb[5] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a8"], dtype=float)
443	    cnb[6] = tsc @ np.asarray(functions["a11"], dtype=float)

397	def assemble_kinetic_blocks_from_coefficients(
398	    *,
399	    c8,
400	    c10,
401	    c11,
402	    radial_grid,
403	    mode_table,
404	    fixed_boundary=True,
405	    igreen=0,
406	    zero_outer_bb=True,
407	):
408	    """Assemble the visible plasma branch of Fortran ``RHSMAT`` from coefficients."""
409	
410	    c8 = np.asarray(c8, dtype=float)
411	    c10 = np.asarray(c10, dtype=float)
412	    c11 = np.asarray(c11, dtype=float)
413	    lmns = mode_table.size
414	    n_intervals = radial_grid.n_intervals
415	    expected = (lmns, lmns, n_intervals)
416	    for name, arr in {"c8": c8, "c10": c10, "c11": c11}.items():
417	        if arr.shape != expected:
418	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {expected}, got {arr.shape}.")
419	    shape = expected
420	    BA = np.zeros(shape)
421	    BB = np.zeros(shape)
422	    BC = np.zeros(shape)
423	    BD = np.zeros(shape)
424	    BE = np.zeros(shape)
425	    BF = np.zeros(shape)
426	    BG = np.zeros(shape)
427	    BH = np.zeros(shape)
428	    BBl = np.zeros(shape)
429	    BBu = np.zeros(shape)
430	    ql = np.asarray(mode_table.ql, dtype=float)
431	    ni = radial_grid.ni
432	    upper_rows, upper_cols = np.triu_indices(lmns)
433	    for interval in range(min(n_intervals, ni)):
434	        si = radial_grid.centers[interval]
435	        dsvar = -ni * radial_grid.ds[interval]
436	        sii = 0.5 / si**ql
437	        siis = np.outer(sii, sii)
438	        bc_upper = dsvar * siis * c8[:, :, interval]
439	        bbl_upper = bc_upper.copy()
440	        be_lc_lr = dsvar * sii[:, None] * c11[:, :, interval]
441	        be_lr_lc = dsvar * sii[None, :] * c11[:, :, interval].T
442	        if interval == 0:
443	            bc_upper = np.zeros_like(bc_upper)
444	            be_lc_lr = np.zeros_like(be_lc_lr)
445	            be_lr_lc = np.zeros_like(be_lr_lc)
446	        BBl[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = bbl_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
447	        BBu[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = bc_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
448	        BC[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = bc_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
449	        BC[upper_cols, upper_rows, interval] = bc_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
450	        BE[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = be_lc_lr[upper_rows, upper_cols]
451	        BE[upper_cols, upper_rows, interval] = be_lr_lc[upper_rows, upper_cols]
452	        BG[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = be_lr_lc[upper_rows, upper_cols]
453	        BG[upper_cols, upper_rows, interval] = be_lc_lr[upper_rows, upper_cols]
454	        bd_upper = dsvar * c10[:, :, interval]
455	        BD[upper_rows, upper_cols, interval] = bd_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
456	        BD[upper_cols, upper_rows, interval] = bd_upper[upper_rows, upper_cols]
457	        BF[:, :, interval] = BE[:, :, interval].T
458	        BA[:, :, interval] = BC[:, :, interval].T
459	        BH[:, :, interval] = BG[:, :, interval].T
460	        if fixed_boundary and interval == ni - 1 and igreen == 0:
461	            BBl[:, :, interval] = 0.0
462	            BC[:, :, interval] = 0.0
463	            BG[:, :, interval] = 0.0
464	            BA[:, :, interval] = 0.0
465	            BH[:, :, interval] = 0.0
466	            BB[:, :, interval] = 0.0
467	    if n_intervals:
468	        BB[:, :, :] = BBl
469	        if n_intervals > 1:
470	            BB[:, :, :-1] += BBu[:, :, 1:]
471	        if zero_outer_bb:
472	            BB[:, :, -1] = 0.0
473	    return TerpsichoreKineticBlocks(
474	        BA=BA, BB=BB, BC=BC, BD=BD, BE=BE, BF=BF, BG=BG, BH=BH, BBl=BBl, BBu=BBu
475	    )

495	def variable_slices(lmns, n_intervals):
496	    """Return global vector slices for TERPSICHORE ``XI`` and ``ETA`` variables."""
497	
498	    xi = [slice(i * lmns, (i + 1) * lmns) for i in range(n_intervals + 1)]
499	    eta_offset = (n_intervals + 1) * lmns
500	    eta = [slice(eta_offset + i * lmns, eta_offset + (i + 1) * lmns) for i in range(n_intervals)]
501	    return xi, eta

504	def assemble_potential_matrix(potential_blocks, radial_grid, mode_table):
505	    """Assemble the global potential matrix used by TERPSICHORE ``ENERGY``.
506	
507	    The matrix satisfies ``x.T @ K @ x == WP`` for a global vector ordered as
508	    ``[XI(0), ..., XI(N), ETA(1), ..., ETA(N)]``.  It follows the symmetrized
509	    quadratic form in Fortran ``ENERGY``.
510	    """
511	
512	    lmns = mode_table.size
513	    n_intervals = radial_grid.n_intervals
514	    dim = (2 * n_intervals + 1) * lmns
515	    K = np.zeros((dim, dim))
516	    xi, eta = variable_slices(lmns, n_intervals)
517	    for interval in range(n_intervals):
518	        i = interval
519	        x0 = np.arange(xi[i].start, xi[i].stop)
520	        x1 = np.arange(xi[i + 1].start, xi[i + 1].stop)
521	        e = np.arange(eta[i].start, eta[i].stop)
522	        _add_quadratic(K, x0, x0, _interval_block(potential_blocks.BU, i))
523	        _add_quadratic(K, x0, e, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.EI, i))
524	        _add_quadratic(K, x0, x1, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.CC, i))
525	        _add_quadratic(K, e, x0, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.FI, i))
526	        _add_quadratic(K, e, e, _interval_block(potential_blocks.DI, i))
527	        _add_quadratic(K, e, x1, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.GI, i))
528	        _add_quadratic(K, x1, x0, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.AI, i))
529	        _add_quadratic(K, x1, e, 0.5 * _interval_block(potential_blocks.HI, i))
530	        _add_quadratic(K, x1, x1, _interval_block(potential_blocks.BL, i))
531	    return K

117	            kinetic_terms[diag].sum() + 2.0 * kinetic_terms[upper_mask].sum()
118	        )
119	    return wp_by_interval, wk_by_interval
120

122	def compute_block_quadratic_energy(xi, eta, potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid):
123	    """Compute ``WP`` and ``WK`` directly from TERPSICHORE blocks.
124	
125	    This is algebraically equivalent to assembling the dense global matrices but
126	    avoids materializing the very large QAS3 matrices during benchmark parity
127	    diagnostics.
128	    """
129	
130	    wp_by_interval, wk_by_interval = compute_block_energy_contributions(
131	        xi, eta, potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid
132	    )
133	    return float(wp_by_interval.sum()), float(wk_by_interval.sum())
134	
135	
136	def compute_fortran_energy_oracle_arrays(
137	    xi, eta, potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid
138	):
139	    """Return arrays in Fortran ``ENERGY`` dump convention.
140	
141	    ``compute_block_energy_contributions`` returns the integrated contribution
142	    to ``WP`` on each interval. Fortran dumps ``WPSI`` before multiplying by
143	    ``dsvar = ni * (s(i) - s(i-1))``, so ``WPSI`` is an interval density.
144	    ``WK_i`` is already an integrated per-interval increment and is returned
145	    unchanged.
146	    """
147	
148	    wp_by_interval, wk_by_interval = compute_block_energy_contributions(
149	        xi, eta, potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid
150	    )
151	    dsvar = radial_grid.ni * np.asarray(radial_grid.ds, dtype=float)
152	    if np.any(dsvar == 0):
153	        raise ValueError("radial grid contains a zero-width interval.")
154	    return {"WPSI": wp_by_interval / dsvar, "WK_i": wk_by_interval}

159	    eta,
160	    potential_blocks,
161	    kinetic_blocks,
162	    radial_grid,
163	    mode_table,
164	    *,
165	    walf=1.0,
166	    diagnostics=None,
167	):
168	    """Compute a stability result from block arrays and split ``XI/ETA``."""
169	
170	    wp, wk = compute_block_quadratic_energy(
171	        xi, eta, potential_blocks, kinetic_blocks, radial_grid
172	    )

174	        wp,
175	        wk,
176	        walf=walf,

178	        eigenvector_eta=np.asarray(eta, dtype=float),
179	        mode_table=mode_table,

191	    *,

8	@dataclass(frozen=True)
9	class TerpsichoreRadialGrid:
10	    """TERPSICHORE-style radial grid in normalized toroidal flux ``s``."""
11	
12	    s_nodes: np.ndarray
13	    ni: int
14	    ivac: int = 0
15	
16	    def __post_init__(self):
17	        s_nodes = np.asarray(self.s_nodes, dtype=float)
18	        if s_nodes.ndim != 1:
19	            raise ValueError("s_nodes must be one-dimensional.")
20	        if s_nodes.size != self.ni + self.ivac + 1:
21	            raise ValueError("s_nodes length must equal ni + ivac + 1.")
22	        if self.ni < 1:
23	            raise ValueError("ni must be positive.")
24	        if self.ivac < 0:
25	            raise ValueError("ivac must be non-negative.")
26	        if np.any(np.diff(s_nodes) <= 0):
27	            raise ValueError("s_nodes must be strictly increasing.")
28	        if not np.isclose(s_nodes[0], 0.0):
29	            raise ValueError("s_nodes must start at 0.")
30	        if not np.isclose(s_nodes[self.ni], 1.0):
31	            raise ValueError("plasma boundary s_nodes[ni] must be 1.")
32	        object.__setattr__(self, "s_nodes", s_nodes)
33	
34	    @property
35	    def n_intervals(self):
36	        return self.ni + self.ivac
37	
38	    @property
39	    def centers(self):
40	        return 0.5 * (self.s_nodes[1:] + self.s_nodes[:-1])
41	
42	    @property
43	    def ds(self):
44	        return np.diff(self.s_nodes)
45	
46	    @property
47	    def plasma_slice(self):
48	        return slice(0, self.ni)
49	
50	    @property
51	    def vacuum_slice(self):
52	        return slice(self.ni, self.ni + self.ivac)
53	
54	    def plasma_view(self):
55	        """Return a grid view containing only plasma intervals."""
56	
57	        return type(self)(s_nodes=self.s_nodes[: self.ni + 1], ni=self.ni, ivac=0)
58	
59	    @classmethod
60	    def uniform(cls, surfs=101, ivac=0, dsvac=0.0):
61	        """Create a uniform plasma mesh plus optional uniform vacuum mesh."""
62	
63	        if surfs < 2:
64	            raise ValueError("surfs must be at least 2.")
65	        ni = surfs - 1
66	        plasma = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, surfs)
67	        if ivac:
68	            vacuum = np.linspace(1.0, 1.0 + dsvac, ivac + 1)[1:]

3	from dataclasses import dataclass
4	
5	import numpy as np
6	
7	
8	@dataclass(frozen=True)
9	class TerpsichoreModeTable:
10	    """Stability perturbation Fourier mode table.
11	
12	    The table stores TERPSICHORE-style poloidal/toroidal mode pairs ``(m, n)``
13	    and axis regularity exponents.  It intentionally keeps a compact data model
14	    so the Fortran ``STABIN`` mode filtering rules can be ported incrementally.
15	    """
16	
17	    m: np.ndarray
18	    n: np.ndarray
19	    mode_family: int = -1
20	    nfp: int = 1
21	    parity: str = "cos"
22	    frozen: np.ndarray | None = None
23	    ql: np.ndarray | None = None
24	
25	    def __post_init__(self):
26	        m = np.asarray(self.m, dtype=int)
27	        n = np.asarray(self.n, dtype=int)
28	        if m.ndim != 1 or n.ndim != 1 or m.shape != n.shape:
29	            raise ValueError("m and n must be one-dimensional arrays with equal length.")
30	        if np.any(m < 0):
31	            raise ValueError("TERPSICHORE poloidal mode numbers must be non-negative.")
32	        if self.nfp <= 0:
33	            raise ValueError("nfp must be positive.")
34	        if self.parity not in {"cos", "sin"}:
35	            raise ValueError("parity must be 'cos' or 'sin'.")
36	        frozen = np.zeros(m.shape, dtype=bool) if self.frozen is None else self.frozen
37	        frozen = np.asarray(frozen, dtype=bool)
38	        if frozen.shape != m.shape:
39	            raise ValueError("frozen must have the same shape as m and n.")
40	        ql = self.axis_regularization(m) if self.ql is None else self.ql
41	        ql = np.asarray(ql, dtype=float)
42	        if ql.shape != m.shape:
43	            raise ValueError("ql must have the same shape as m and n.")
44	        object.__setattr__(self, "m", m)
45	        object.__setattr__(self, "n", n)
46	        object.__setattr__(self, "frozen", frozen)
47	        object.__setattr__(self, "ql", ql)
48	
49	    @property
50	    def size(self):
51	        """Number of retained stability modes."""
52	
53	        return self.m.size
54	
55	    @property
56	    def modes(self):
57	        """Return an ``(size, 2)`` array of ``(m, n)`` mode pairs."""
58	
59	        return np.column_stack((self.m, self.n))
60	
61	    @staticmethod
62	    def axis_regularization(m):
63	        """Return TERPSICHORE-compatible axis exponents for ``XI``.
64	
65	        The full Fortran implementation contains additional parity-dependent
66	        details.  This migration-safe default captures the documented behavior:
67	        non-``m=1`` modes vanish on axis, while ``m=1`` uses the special scaled
68	        regularity branch.
69	        """
70	
71	        m = np.asarray(m, dtype=int)
72	        return np.where(m == 1, 0.5, np.maximum(m, 1)).astype(float)
73	
74	    @classmethod
75	    def from_bounds(
76	        cls,
77	        *,
78	        M_max=8,
79	        N_min=-4,
80	        N_max=4,
81	        mode_family=-1,
82	        nfp=1,
83	        parity="cos",
84	    ):
85	        """Build a mode table from DESC-native bounds.
86	
87	        For ``mode_family < 0`` this includes every ``n`` in ``[N_min, N_max]``.
88	        Otherwise it retains toroidal modes satisfying the TERPSICHORE family
89	        relation ``n = i * nfp ± mode_family``.
90	        """
91	
92	        if M_max < 0:
93	            raise ValueError("M_max must be non-negative.")
94	        if N_min > N_max:
95	            raise ValueError("N_min must be <= N_max.")
96	        if nfp <= 0:
97	            raise ValueError("nfp must be positive.")
98	        modes = []
99	        for n in range(N_min, N_max + 1):
100	            if mode_family >= 0:
101	                remainder = abs(n) % nfp
102	                family = min(remainder, nfp - remainder)
103	                if family != mode_family:
104	                    continue
105	            for m in range(M_max + 1):
106	                modes.append((m, n))
107	        if not modes:
108	            raise ValueError("mode bounds produced an empty TERPSICHORE mode table.")
109	        arr = np.asarray(modes, dtype=int)
110	        return cls(
111	            arr[:, 0],
112	            arr[:, 1],
113	            mode_family=mode_family,
114	            nfp=nfp,
115	            parity=parity,
116	        )

2	
3	from dataclasses import dataclass
4	
5	import numpy as np
6	
7	
8	@dataclass(frozen=True)
9	class TerpsichoreTrigTable:
10	    """STABIN/cospol-style trigonometric lookup table for stability modes."""
11	
12	    lsx: dict
13	    msx: np.ndarray
14	    nsx: np.ndarray
15	    tss: np.ndarray
16	    tsc: np.ndarray
17	    pol: np.ndarray
18	    tor: np.ndarray
19	    nper: int
20	
21	    @property
22	    def lss(self):
23	        return self.msx.size
24	
25	    def lookup(self, m, n_reduced, parity=0):
26	        return self.lsx[(int(m), int(n_reduced), int(parity))]
27	
28	
29	def _fortran_divisible(value, nper):
30	    return value - int(value / nper) * nper == 0
31	
32	
33	def build_lsx_lookup(mode_table, nper):
34	    """Build TERPSICHORE ``lsx/msx/nsx`` lookup for difference and sum modes."""
35	
36	    if nper <= 0:
37	        raise ValueError("nper must be positive.")
38	    ms = np.asarray(mode_table.m, dtype=int)
39	    ns = np.asarray(mode_table.n, dtype=int)
40	    lsx = {}
41	    msx = []
42	    nsx = []
43	    seen = set()
44	    for sign in (-1, 1):
45	        for lc in range(mode_table.size):
46	            for lr in range(mode_table.size):
47	                mval = int(ms[lc] + sign * ms[lr])
48	                nval = int(ns[lc] + sign * ns[lr])
49	                if not _fortran_divisible(nval, nper):
50	                    continue
51	                n_reduced = int(nval / nper)
52	                key = (mval, n_reduced)
53	                if key in seen:
54	                    continue
55	                seen.add(key)
56	                msx.append(mval)
57	                nsx.append(nval)
58	                # Store Fortran-style packed indices. Index 0 is a zero-valued
59	                # sentinel in CNA/CNB/TSS/TSC, while physical modes start at 1.
60	                # Fortran only fills parity 0; parity 1 remains the zero
61	                # sentinel used when sums/differences are not divisible by nper.
62	                lsx[(mval, n_reduced, 0)] = len(msx)
63	                lsx.setdefault((mval, n_reduced, 1), 0)
64	    return lsx, np.asarray(msx, dtype=int), np.asarray(nsx, dtype=int)
65	
66	
67	def build_poloidal_toroidal_grid(nj, nk, nper, tpi=2 * np.pi):
68	    """Build TERPSICHORE ``POL`` and ``TOR`` arrays using cospol indexing."""
69	
70	    if nj <= 0 or nk <= 0 or nper <= 0:
71	        raise ValueError("nj, nk and nper must be positive.")
72	    njk = nj * nk
73	    dth = 1.0 / nj
74	    dph = 1.0 / nk
75	    pol = np.empty(njk)
76	    tor = np.empty(njk)
77	    for jk in range(njk):
78	        pol[jk] = tpi * dth * (jk % nj)
79	        tor[jk] = tpi * dph * (jk // nj) / nper
80	    return pol, tor
81	
82	
83	def build_trig_table(mode_table, *, nj, nk, nper, pol=None, tor=None):
84	    """Build ``TSS``/``TSC`` tables for FOURIN native coefficient generation."""
85	
86	    lsx, msx, nsx = build_lsx_lookup(mode_table, nper=nper)
87	    if pol is None or tor is None:
88	        pol, tor = build_poloidal_toroidal_grid(nj, nk, nper)
89	    else:
90	        pol = np.asarray(pol, dtype=float)
91	        tor = np.asarray(tor, dtype=float)
92	        if pol.shape != tor.shape:
93	            raise ValueError("pol and tor must have the same shape.")
94	    lss = len(msx)
95	    tss = np.zeros((lss + 1, pol.size))
96	    tsc = np.zeros((lss + 1, pol.size))
97	    for idx, (mval, nval) in enumerate(zip(msx, nsx), start=1):
98	        phase = mval * pol - nval * tor
99	        tss[idx] = np.sin(phase)
100	        tsc[idx] = np.cos(phase)
101	    return TerpsichoreTrigTable(
102	        lsx=lsx, msx=msx, nsx=nsx, tss=tss, tsc=tsc, pol=pol, tor=tor, nper=nper
103	    )

```python
def _project_outer_shell_integrals_to_modal_coefficients(
    *, cna, cnb, mode_table, nper, lsx, dtdp, cospar
):
    """Project reduced outer-shell ``cna``/``cnb`` integrals to modal coefficients."""
    cna = np.asarray(cna, dtype=float)
    cnb = np.asarray(cnb, dtype=float)
    if cna.shape != cnb.shape or cna.ndim != 3:
        raise ValueError("cna and cnb must be rank-3 arrays with identical shape.")
    if cna.shape[0] < 4:
        raise ValueError("outer-shell cna/cnb first dimension must include indices 1..3.")
    lmns = mode_table.size
    intervals = cna.shape[2]
    shape = (lmns, lmns, intervals)
    coeffs = {name: np.zeros(shape) for name in ALL_COEFFICIENTS}
    indices = compute_fourin_mapping_indices(mode_table, nper=nper, lsx=lsx)
    ld = indices["ld"]
    lp = indices["lp"]
    for interval in range(intervals):
        coeffs["c1"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cna[1, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[1, lp, interval]
        )
        coeffs["c2"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cna[2, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[2, lp, interval]
        )
        coeffs["c3"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cna[3, ld, interval] - cospar * cna[3, lp, interval]
        )
        coeffs["c4"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cnb[1, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[1, lp, interval]
        )
        coeffs["c5"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cnb[2, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[2, lp, interval]
        )
        coeffs["c6"][:, :, interval] = dtdp * (
            cnb[3, ld, interval] + cospar * cnb[3, lp, interval]
        )
    return TerpsichoreCoefficientData(coefficients=coeffs, fixed_boundary=False)
```

def _project_outer_shell_integrals_to_modal_coefficients(
    *, cna, cnb, mode_table, nper, lsx, dtdp, cospar
):
    """Project reduced outer-shell ``cna``/``cnb`` integrals to modal coefficients.

    Ports the vacuum branch of Fortran ``FOURIN``: the six non-zero outer-shell
    integrals (``gppl``, ``gtpl``, ``gttl`` in ``cna``; ``gstl``, ``gssl``,
    ``gssu`` in ``cnb``) are folded with the ``lsx`` sum/difference lookup into
    the wall-sensitive modal coefficients ``c1..c6``, mirroring how the plasma
    branch maps its integrals onto ``c0..c7``.  Odd-parity (sin) tables pair
    with ``dtdp * (ld - cospar * lp)`` on the ``cna`` bank and even-parity
    (cos) tables with ``dtdp * (ld + cospar * lp)`` on the ``cnb`` bank.
    """

    cna = np.asarray(cna, dtype=float)
    cnb = np.asarray(cnb, dtype=float)
    if cna.shape != cnb.shape or cna.ndim != 3:
        raise ValueError("cna and cnb must be rank-3 arrays with identical shape.")
    if cna.shape[0] < 4:
        raise ValueError("outer-shell cna/cnb first dimension must include indices 1..3.")
    lmns = mode_table.size
    intervals = cna.shape[2]
    shape = (lmns, lmns, intervals)
    coeffs = {name: np.zeros(shape) for name in ALL_COEFFICIENTS}
    indices = compute_fourin_mapping_indices(mode_table, nper=nper, lsx=lsx)
    ld = indices["ld"]
    lp = indices["lp"]
    coeffs["c1"] = dtdp * (cna[1, ld] - cospar * cna[1, lp])
    coeffs["c2"] = dtdp * (cna[2, ld] - cospar * cna[2, lp])
    coeffs["c3"] = dtdp * (cna[3, ld] - cospar * cna[3, lp])
    coeffs["c4"] = dtdp * (cnb[1, ld] + cospar * cnb[1, lp])
    coeffs["c5"] = dtdp * (cnb[2, ld] + cospar * cnb[2, lp])
    coeffs["c6"] = dtdp * (cnb[3, ld] + cospar * cnb[3, lp])
    return TerpsichoreCoefficientData(coefficients=coeffs, fixed_boundary=False)

"""Sanity checks for the wall-coupled external-region capability (not committed)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("/workspace/task/source")))

from desc.stability.terpsichore.demo_case import build_demo_case, build_wall_variants
from desc.stability.terpsichore.external_region import build_external_region_payload
from desc.stability.terpsichore.assembly import (
    assemble_potential_matrix,
    assemble_kinetic_matrix,
    concatenate_potential_blocks,
)
from desc.stability.terpsichore.energy import (
    compute_block_quadratic_energy,
    compute_energy_from_vector,
    split_global_vector,
)
from desc.stability.terpsichore.outer_region import (
    assemble_outer_region_response_payload,
    build_outer_region_metric_payload,
    build_outer_region_operator_payload,
)
from desc.stability.terpsichore.equilibrium import vacmet_inputs_from_equilibrium_data
from desc.stability.terpsichore.vacuum import compute_vacmet_metrics
from desc.stability.terpsichore.radial import TerpsichoreRadialGrid
from desc.stability.terpsichore.modes import TerpsichoreModeTable
from desc.stability.terpsichore.trig import build_trig_table


def build_case(surfs=4, ivac=2, dsvac=0.7, nj=3, nk=2, M_max=1, N_min=0, N_max=0):
    case = build_demo_case()  # base equilibrium data reuse
    radial_grid = TerpsichoreRadialGrid.uniform(surfs=surfs, ivac=ivac, dsvac=dsvac)
    mode_table = TerpsichoreModeTable.from_bounds(
        M_max=M_max, N_min=N_min, N_max=N_max, nfp=1, parity="cos"
    )
    return case, radial_grid, mode_table, build_trig_table(mode_table, nj=nj, nk=nk, nper=1)


failures = []


def check(name, cond):
    print(("PASS" if cond else "FAIL"), name)
    if not cond:
        failures.append(name)


# 1. Public demo setup: masked block energy == dense global matrix energy.
case = build_demo_case()
eq = case["equilibrium_data"]
wall_a, wall_b = build_wall_variants(eq, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
payload = build_external_region_payload(
    eq, mode_table=case["mode_table"], trig_table=case["trig_table"],
    xi=case["xi"], eta=case["eta"], wall=wall_a, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1,
)
wpA = payload["result"].wp
# Recompute via dense matrices from concatenated blocks.
inputs = vacmet_inputs_from_equilibrium_data(eq, wall=wall_a, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
vacmet = compute_vacmet_metrics(**inputs)
vgd = vacmet.as_vacuum_grid_data()
metric = build_outer_region_metric_payload(equilibrium_data=eq, vacuum_grid_data=vgd)
operator = build_outer_region_operator_payload(
    metric_payload=metric, mode_table=case["mode_table"],
    trig_table=case["trig_table"], radial_grid=eq.radial_grid,
)
resp = assemble_outer_region_response_payload(
    metric_payload=metric, operator_payload=operator,
    mode_table=case["mode_table"], radial_grid=eq.radial_grid,
)
rg = eq.radial_grid
from desc.stability.terpsichore.assembly import (
    assemble_potential_blocks_from_coefficients,
    assemble_kinetic_blocks_from_coefficients,
    concatenate_kinetic_blocks,
    _zero_outer_shell_kinetic_blocks,
)
from desc.stability.terpsichore.external_region import _plasma_grid, _legacy_coefficients

plasma_coeffs = _legacy_coefficients(eq.data["terpsichore_coefficients"])
plasma_potential = assemble_potential_blocks_from_coefficients(
    **{k: plasma_coeffs[k] for k in ("c0", "c1", "c2", "c4", "c5", "c6", "c9",
                                     "ftp", "fpp", "ftpp", "fppp", "ci", "cj")},
    radial_grid=_plasma_grid(rg), mode_table=case["mode_table"],
    fixed_boundary=False, igreen=plasma_coeffs.get("igreen", 0),
)
plasma_kinetic = assemble_kinetic_blocks_from_coefficients(
    **{k: plasma_coeffs[k] for k in ("c8", "c10", "c11")},
    radial_grid=_plasma_grid(rg), mode_table=case["mode_table"],
    fixed_boundary=False, igreen=plasma_coeffs.get("igreen", 0), zero_outer_bb=False,
)
full_potential = concatenate_potential_blocks(plasma_potential, resp.potential_blocks)
full_kinetic = concatenate_kinetic_blocks(plasma_kinetic, _zero_outer_shell_kinetic_blocks(rg, case["mode_table"]))
K = assemble_potential_matrix(full_potential, rg, case["mode_table"])
M = assemble_kinetic_matrix(full_kinetic, rg, case["mode_table"])
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
xi_r = rng.normal(size=case["xi"].shape)
eta_r = rng.normal(size=case["eta"].shape)
# global vector assembly: [XI nodes..., ETA intervals...] with mode-major ordering
n_int = rg.n_intervals
lmns = case["mode_table"].size
vec = np.concatenate([xi_r.T.reshape(-1), eta_r.T.reshape(-1)])
xi_s, eta_s = split_global_vector(vec, rg, case["mode_table"])
wp_masked, wk_masked = compute_block_quadratic_energy(xi_s, eta_s, full_potential, full_kinetic, rg)
res = compute_energy_from_vector(vec, full_potential, full_kinetic, rg, case["mode_table"])
print(f"masked wp={wp_masked:.6e}, dense wp={res.wp:.6e}")
check("masked vs dense K potential energy match", np.isclose(wp_masked, res.wp, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-9))
print(f"masked wk={wk_masked:.6e}, dense wk={res.wk:.6e}")
check("masked vs dense M kinetic energy match", np.isclose(wk_masked, res.wk, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-9))

# 2. Wall changes vacuum intervals only; plasma intervals invariant.
pay_b = build_external_region_payload(
    eq, mode_table=case["mode_table"], trig_table=case["trig_table"],
    xi=case["xi"], eta=case["eta"], wall=wall_b, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1,
)
ni = rg.ni
same_plasma = np.allclose(payload["wp_by_interval"][:ni], pay_b["wp_by_interval"][:ni])
diff_vac = not np.allclose(payload["wp_by_interval"][ni:], pay_b["wp_by_interval"][ni:])
check("plasma intervals invariant across walls", same_plasma)
check("vacuum intervals respond to wall", diff_vac)
print("wp_by_interval wall_a:", payload["wp_by_interval"])
print("wp_by_interval wall_b:", pay_b["wp_by_interval"])

# 3. Coefficients/blocks carry wall sensitivity at each chain level.
inputs_b = vacmet_inputs_from_equilibrium_data(eq, wall=wall_b, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
vacmet_b = compute_vacmet_metrics(**inputs_b)
check("vacmet metrics respond to wall", not np.allclose(vacmet.bjac, vacmet_b.bjac))
metric_b = build_outer_region_metric_payload(equilibrium_data=eq, vacuum_grid_data=vacmet_b.as_vacuum_grid_data())
operator_b = build_outer_region_operator_payload(
    metric_payload=metric_b, mode_table=case["mode_table"],
    trig_table=case["trig_table"], radial_grid=rg,
)
check("cna responds to wall", not np.allclose(operator.cna, operator_b.cna))
resp_b = assemble_outer_region_response_payload(
    metric_payload=metric_b, operator_payload=operator_b,
    mode_table=case["mode_table"], radial_grid=rg,
)
check("modal coefficients respond to wall", not np.allclose(resp.coefficients["c1"], resp_b.coefficients["c1"]))
check("potential blocks respond to wall", not np.allclose(np.asarray(resp.potential_blocks.BU), np.asarray(resp_b.potential_blocks.BU)))

# 4. Generic grids/mode sets and both nowall signs: finite, wall-distinct.
for kw in [dict(surfs=3, ivac=1, dsvac=0.4), dict(surfs=5, ivac=3, dsvac=0.9),
           dict(M_max=1, N_min=-1, N_max=1, nj=4, nk=3)]:
    c2, rg2, mt2, tt2 = build_case(**kw)
    eq2 = c2["equilibrium_data"]
    object.__setattr__(eq2.radial_grid, "_dummy", None)  # noop
    # rebuild equilibrium wrapper with new radial grid
    from desc.stability.terpsichore.equilibrium import TerpsichoreEquilibriumData
    data = dict(eq2.data)
    if rg2.ni != eq2.radial_grid.ni:
        # plasma coefficients are sized to ni=3; regenerate stack for other ni
        from desc.stability.terpsichore.demo_case import _plasma_coefficients
        data["terpsichore_coefficients"] = _plasma_coefficients(mt2, rg2)
        data["terpsichore_ftp_edge"] = data["terpsichore_coefficients"]["ftp"][-1]
        data["terpsichore_fpp_edge"] = data["terpsichore_coefficients"]["fpp"][-1]
    eq2 = TerpsichoreEquilibriumData(grid=None, radial_grid=rg2, data=data)
    xi2 = rng.normal(size=(mt2.size, rg2.n_intervals + 1))
    eta2 = rng.normal(size=(mt2.size, rg2.n_intervals))
    wa, wb = build_wall_variants(eq2, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
    p_a = build_external_region_payload(eq2, mode_table=mt2, trig_table=tt2,
                                        xi=xi2, eta=eta2, wall=wa, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
    p_b = build_external_region_payload(eq2, mode_table=mt2, trig_table=tt2,
                                        xi=xi2, eta=eta2, wall=wb, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
    p_now = build_external_region_payload(eq2, mode_table=mt2, trig_table=tt2,
                                          xi=xi2, eta=eta2, wall=None, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=-1)
    vals = [p_a["result"].wp, p_a["result"].omega2, p_a["result"].growth_rate,
            p_b["result"].wp, p_now["result"].wp, p_now["result"].omega2]
    check(f"generic case {kw} finite", np.all(np.isfinite(vals)))
    check(f"generic case {kw} walls distinct", not np.allclose(p_a["result"].wp, p_b["result"].wp))

# 5. ivac=0 internal-only path no-ops.
rg0 = TerpsichoreRadialGrid.uniform(surfs=4, ivac=0)
data0 = dict(eq.data)
eq0 = TerpsichoreEquilibriumData(grid=None, radial_grid=rg0, data=data0)
mt0 = case["mode_table"]
tt0 = build_trig_table(mt0, nj=3, nk=2, nper=1)
xi0 = case["xi"][:, : rg0.n_intervals + 1]
eta0 = case["eta"][:, : rg0.n_intervals]
p0 = build_external_region_payload(eq0, mode_table=mt0, trig_table=tt0,
                                   xi=xi0, eta=eta0, wall=wall_a, wall_scale=1.3, nowall=1)
pd0 = build_external_region_payload(eq0, mode_table=mt0, trig_table=tt0,

print()
print("FAILURES:", failures if failures else "none")
sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

- `coefficients.py` — implemented the FOURIN vacuum projection: the six outer-shell integrals (`gppl`, `gtpl`, `gttl` in `cna`; `gstl`, `gssl`, `gssu` in `cnb`) are folded through the `lsx`/`ld`/`lp` sum-difference lookup into `c1..c6` with the same bank/sign convention as the plasma branch (`dtdp·(ld − cospar·lp)` for `cna`, `dtdp·(ld + cospar·lp)` for `cnb`), fully array-based.
- `assembly.py` — implemented the outer-shell LHSMAT branch: per pseudo-vacuum interval, wall-sensitive Dirichlet-form blocks — even-parity angular kernels from `c1..c3` with the flux-labelled field-line weights (`fppfpp·m m′`, `−ftpfpp/2·(m n′ + n m′)`, `ftpftp·n n′`), radial roof-derivative couplings from `c5`, and telescoped mixed `s-θ`/`s-ζ` fluxes from `c4`/`c6` on the node-cross pair, keeping the existing frozen-wall boundary condition on the outermost interval and the negated fill convention so the blocks are consistent in both the interval-energy and dense-global-matrix reductions.
